content.tldr: An Iceberg snapshot represents the complete state of a table at a specific point in time, defined by an immutable manifest list referencing all active data files.
content.simple_explanation: Every commit to an Iceberg table (append, overwrite, delete) creates a new immutable snapshot. A snapshot contains a manifest list file, which enumerates all the manifest files that compose the table at that commit. Because past snapshots are never altered, queries are guaranteed repeatable read isolation: a reader pinned to snapshot ID 1234 will always see identical records, even while concurrent jobs commit millions of new rows under snapshot ID 1235.
content.real_world_example: A Git commit tree: each Git commit represents an immutable snapshot of your entire codebase; you can inspect the current master branch while another developer checks out a previous commit hash without interference.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Accumulating thousands of snapshots causes metadata bloat and holds unreferenced data files indefinitely. Data engineers must run automated snapshot expiration procedures (`expire_snapshots`) to reclaim storage and prune stale manifests.
